publisherConventions: Before March 2015 each processed window produced a separate FITS file; from March 2015 the pipeline merges windows from the same observation. This describes processing history, not a new observation date.
Non-missing newly merged data overwrite old data; the table records window processing and pixel mismatches.
Header data-key suffixes are sorted and re-sorted; suffix order is not processing order. Duplicate data keys are removed.
Each merged window generates at least one row with offsets -999 and delta zero. The document explicitly says those sentinel rows do not indicate merge anomalies.
WINDOWW and WINDOWH are compression subframe width and height parameters. Windows concern downloaded pixels, not mosaicking; no single window necessarily defines all valid image pixels.
GRT means ground-received time; ARCHDATE refers to packet telemetry filename. Neither is independently an observation timestamp.

elaraCrosswalk.observedPreviously: Both raw products have one table row, offsets -999, delta zero, WINDOWW 1028 and WINDOWH zero.
elaraCrosswalk.supportedInterpretation: The sentinel offsets and zero delta are consistent with the documented bookkeeping row and are not by themselves evidence of a merge anomaly.
elaraCrosswalk.unresolved: The document gives no zero-height special-case rule. WINDOWH zero must remain unexplained; do not infer an empty image, complete coverage, successful pipeline reconstruction, or repair it.

This document provides some explanation regarding the use of
                subframes in some New Horizons instrument data (MVIC, LEISA,
                and LORRI) as well as the source and significance of the
                "Window Mismatches" table included in some raw data	products.
                "Windows", in this case, refers to pixels downloaded at various
                times, rather than a mosaicking process. No single "window"
                necessarily defines	all pixels with data in the image.
